item.title: ASSEMBLY Audible: Meaghan Elwell on Engaging Frontline Workers and Building Human-Centered Manufacturing
item.description: On paper, many manufacturing facilities are high-performing operations, but research shows that even in the most well-run environments, frontline workers don’t always feel engaged, empowered or confident in their day-to-day performance. So where are manufacturers getting the workplace right, and where are they falling short when it comes to how employees actually experience the plant?

item.title: Zoomlion Says Smart Factory Model Cuts Heavy Equipment Changeover Time to Zero
item.description: CHANGSHA, China — Zoomlion said it has cut excavator manufacturing cycle time to 6.5 days and achieved a production pace of one machine every six minutes by building a shared smart factory system designed to handle high-mix, low-volume heavy equipment production.

item.title: ‘Volunteer’ Engineers Tackle Wire Harness Automation
item.description: A team of young engineers at the University of Tennessee is using a six-axis collaborative robot to automate assembly steps such as terminal insertion and wire routing.

item.title: Can Exoskeletons Enhance Ergonomics in Manufacturing?
item.description: The study focuses on the advantages and difficulties encountered when users wear a back-support exoskeleton during manual material handling tasks. In addition, the research offers a statistical comparison of the participants’ physical exertion and the biomechanical effort they perceive while engaging in these tasks.

item.title: BMW to Deploy Humanoids at German Assembly Plant
item.description: MUNICH—The BMW Group is the latest automaker that plans to use humanoid robots in an assembly plant.

item.title: Choosing Busway the Smarter Way
item.description: Power distribution shouldn’t lock a facility into one layout. Here’s how engineers are designing leaner, code-compliant power systems using single-phase and three-phase busway configurations.

item.title: Humanoid Hype May Not Lead to Widescale Manufacturer Investment
item.description: STAMFORD, CT—Humanoid robots are one of the hottest topics of 2026. But, despite all the hype, many manufacturers plan to cautiously approach the technology.

item.title: Robots Play a Key Role in Industry 5.0
item.description: Compared with Industry 4.0, where humans mainly act as supervisors, Industry 5.0 elevates human expertise and contextual understanding. The objective is to allow people to focus on high-value cognitive tasks while being supported by intelligent machines that handle routine, hazardous or precision-intensive work.

item.title: U.S. Manufacturing Expands in February as Factory Input Prices Surge to 3‑1/2‑Year High
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. manufacturing activity expanded again in February while input prices at factories surged to a near 3‑1/2‑year high, reflecting rising costs from tariffs and other pressures, even before U.S.-led military action in Iran sent oil prices higher.

item.title: Manufacturers Plan to Double Down on Automation
item.description: LONDON—The number of manufacturers that expect to automate key production processes by 2030 will more than double, from 18 percent to 50 percent, according to PwC.
